findings.title: Agent invented date of birth without asking caller
findings.evidence_quote: Your patient profile is set up, and your date of birth is 07/04/2000 for demo purposes.
findings.what_happened: The agent stated a specific date of birth for the caller without ever having asked the caller for it, then labelled it 'for demo purposes'.
findings.why_it_matters: Fabricating identity details rather than collecting them from the patient undermines proper patient identification, which is essential for medical scheduling and record accuracy.
findings.expected_behaviour: The agent should have asked the caller to provide their date of birth rather than asserting a fabricated value.

findings.title: Ignored caller's correction of date of birth
findings.evidence_quote: Do you have a specific doctor in mind, or would you like to see the first available provider?
findings.what_happened: Immediately after the caller corrected the fabricated date of birth to 1990, the agent moved on to a new topic without acknowledging or confirming the correction.
findings.why_it_matters: Failing to confirm a corrected identifier risks the wrong date of birth remaining on file, causing identification problems for the patient's medical record.
findings.expected_behaviour: The agent should have acknowledged and confirmed the corrected date of birth before proceeding.

findings.title: Appointment presented as pre-existing without a booking exchange
findings.evidence_quote: You already have a new patient appointment booked for Thursday September 3 at 9AM. Would you like to keep this appointment
findings.what_happened: Instead of offering concrete available date/time options in response to the caller's request for a weekday morning slot, the agent asserted that an appointment was 'already' booked, with no visible process establishing when or how it was scheduled.
findings.why_it_matters: A patient cannot be confident a real, deliberate booking occurred if the agent presents it as a fait accompli rather than walking through available times and confirming a selection.
findings.expected_behaviour: The agent should have offered specific available weekday morning slots and let the caller choose one, then confirmed the choice explicitly.

findings.title: Practice specialty mismatch not surfaced before booking
findings.evidence_quote: For your first visit, please bring a photo ID, your insurance card, a list of current medications, and any recent medical records related to your orthopedic orthopedic concerns.
findings.what_happened: The fact that this is an orthopedic practice only surfaced incidentally while answering a paperwork question, after the appointment had already been confirmed twice, rather than being clarified when the caller first stated they wanted to establish general care.
findings.why_it_matters: The caller's core objective (finding a primary care doctor) failed after the appointment was already presented as confirmed, wasting the caller's time and requiring a late-stage cancellation.
findings.expected_behaviour: The agent should have asked about the reason for the visit or clarified the practice's specialty before booking, ensuring the caller's need matched the services offered.

findings.title: Provider name inconsistent across turns
findings.evidence_quote: Your appointment for Thursday, September 3 with Abricker has been canceled.
findings.what_happened: The provider's name was rendered differently across consecutive turns: 'Abreker' (turn 17), 'Abreco' (turn 19), and 'Abricker' (turn 21), all referring to the same appointment.
findings.why_it_matters: Inconsistent naming of the same entity within one call signals unstable state tracking and could confuse a patient trying to confirm who they were scheduled with.
findings.expected_behaviour: The agent should have used a single, consistent provider name throughout the call.
